historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission decided to build an enclosed swimming pool at Balboa Park instead of at Aquatic Park, moving the bond money and the architects Frederick H. Reimers and Paul C. Overmire to the new site.

The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract to convert the old Ingleside police stables in Balboa Park into an athletic clubhouse, with showers and dressing rooms for teams, to Oscar Fresco and Sons at $115,920, on plans by the architect J. A. Riddell.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved the final plans by the architect Frederick H. Reimers for the Balboa Park swimming pool and recreation center, estimated at $415,085, subject to the Art Commission.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract to build the Balboa Park recreation center and pool to Engstrum & Nourse at $422,300, subject to funds, the lowest of seven bids.

At the Old Timers Baseball Association's suggestion, the Recreation and Park Commission named the two baseball diamonds at Balboa Park the August Sundberg Diamond and the Maurice J. Sweeney Diamond, for two men who had given their lives to youth and junior baseball, and ordered markers placed.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract for bleachers at the Balboa Park soccer stadium to C. J. Collins Co. and Wellnitz & DeNarde, joint venturers, at $224,608.
